paragraphs.text: Sync DSH profiles, plugin manifests, and skills between Macs through iCloud Drive.
# dsh-icloud-sync

Keep your DeepSeek Harness setup in step across Macs through iCloud Drive — profiles, plugin
manifes

ts, skills — with a **Settings → Integrations** panel, a **云端** tab next to 任务 / 频道
that pushes and

pulls single session snapshots on demand, and a CLI bundled inside the package. A
fresh Mac needs no
terminal: install the plugin, open the panel, click **从云端接入**.
## What it syncs
Synced, from `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/` plus skills:
- `cordis.patch.yml`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `.dsh-market/state.js

on`
- `~/.agents/skills/**`

Session logs are **not** part of that bundle: upload them from the conversation's own action strip
(

上传到 iCloud, next to 复制 / 好的回答 / 有问题的回答) and download or delete them from the 云端 tab
(see below).

Project workspaces travel the same way, but whole: 上传项目 sends every session of the project plus
the
entire directory tree (files, subfolders, symlinks, permission bits, incrementally by SHA-256), and

下载项目 restores that tree byte-for-byte at the recorded path — so the other Mac can open the same
fold
er and keep working, not just reread the conversation.

Never synced: `node_modules`, runtimes, caches, stored credentials, the DSH app itself. Plugins
rein
stall from `package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` on each Mac.
## How it stays safe

- The cloud holds one bundle: `DSH-Sync/current/` (files plus `manifest.tsv`).
- Every Mac keeps a `

base` copy in `~/.dsh/.icloud-sync/base/`, the last state both sides agreed on.
- Each run compares

local / cloud / base, so "only local changed", "only cloud changed", and "both
changed" are distingu

ishable. When both changed the run refuses to overwrite; review with
`dsh-sync diff` and then `push

--force` or `pull --force`.
- `manifest.tsv` is written last, so half-downloaded iCloud files never

look like deletions.
- Every push/pull backs up first: 20 local copies, 30 cloud copies.
## Session sync（conversation strip + 云端 tab）

The session rail has four tabs: **任务**, **频道**, **云端**, **日程**. Syncing is manual and split in
two.

**Uploading** starts inside the conversation itself: open a session, and the assistant action
strip

(the row with 复制 / 好的回答 / 有问题的回答) carries an 上传到 iCloud button, available as soon
as the project is

not running. The **云端** tab is the iCloud side: it lists only the sessions that
exist in iCloud and
offers 下载 and 删除云端. Sessions that live only on this Mac never show up there.

The same upload is also in the project's right-click menu (right-click a project in the sidebar →
**
上传项目到 iCloud**); it runs in the background and reports the result in a small toast.
Rows are grouped by project, and every group header carries **上传项目** and **下载项目**:

- **上传项目** uploads every session of that project this Mac has, including the ones iCloud has never
s

een (the header shows how many are 未上传), then the project directory itself: every file, subfolder,
s

ymlink and permission bit, incrementally by SHA-256 (`.DS_Store` is skipped, files over 4 GB are
rep

orted and left out). Live sessions contribute their already-persisted messages.
- **下载项目** downloads

every cloud copy of that project that is newer than the local one; copies that
are already identica

l are left alone, and running sessions are skipped instead of failing the batch.
It then restores th

e project tree from `manifest.json` (identical files are left untouched, anything
replaced is first

archived under `DSH-Sync/history/projects/`). If the other Mac uses another user
name, `/Users/<them
>/…` is remapped to this Mac's home directory.

- Every row shows title, project, last activity, size and one of four states: 已上传 / 未上传 /
云端更新 / 仅云端

.
- **上传到 iCloud** overwrites the cloud snapshot of that session; the previous snapshot moves to
`DS

H-Sync/history/sessions/<timestamp>-<machine>/` and is never deleted. Uploading a session that
is st

ill open snapshots only the messages already written to disk.
[该节后续省略]
### The 云端 tab needs a tiny codex-ui patch

The sidebar is drawn by `@michengai/dsh-codex-ui`, which hardcodes its 任务 / 频道 / 日程 tabs, so a
third

-party plugin cannot add a tab through the public slot API. On first start this plugin therefore
app

lies one small, reversible local patch to that package (`lib/codex-sidebar-tab.js`): it declares a
`
sidebar.cloud` slot and renders its occupants as one more companion tab. Nothing else in codex-ui is
touched, the patched bundle is syntax-checked before it is written, and the untouched original stay

s
at `lib/client.js.before-dsh-cloud`.
- The patch is re-applied automatically after a codex-ui upgrade, and skipped (with a warning) if th

e
anchors changed — a skipped patch only loses the tab, never the plugin.
- `dsh-sync codex-tab stat

us` shows whether it is applied; `dsh-sync codex-tab revert` restores the
original file. Both work w

ithout restarting DSH.
- To stop using the patch entirely, run the revert command or remove the call

in `index.js`; the
settings panel and CLI keep working either way.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package ships straight from GitHub (`github:mkoalade/dsh-icloud-sync`), so the `github:` form
ab

ove is the canonical one — pnpm in the profile takes git specifiers as-is. Replace `desktop` with
yo

ur profile name. Restart DSH if the panel does not appear; it lives at
**Settings → Integrations → i

name. Restart DSH if the panel does not appear; it lives at
**Settings → Integrations → iCloud 同步**.

The package ships its own patch row, so installation mounts the plugin — there is no second step
and
no `~/.local/bin` requirement, because the CLI is bundled as `bin/dsh-sync`.
## First Mac: publish your setup
Quit DSH completely first, then use the panel (**创建同步包** / **立即同步**) or the CLI:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`init` also copies the script to `DSH-Sync/bin/dsh-sync`, so another Mac can bootstrap from iCloud
w
ithout this package.
## Requirements

macOS with iCloud Drive enabled, a DSH profile that has started at least once, and the same or a
nea
rby DSH version on each Mac. The CLI is bash 3.2-compatible and needs no runtime.
